title: Run Khidma locally and view its citizen and reviewer screens
intent: Anyone can see what Khidma does by running one command and clicking through the citizen and reviewer screens. The screens drive the real lifecycle module, never a mock, so what they show is what the code does.

outcomes.title: One command starts a local HTTP server that exposes the request lifecycle over JSON routes, backed by the in-memory store.
A citizen screen and a reviewer screen in the browser call those routes and show every status, with a basic consistent layout.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: One documented npm command starts the server on a local port. No install step is needed beyond npm install.
JSON routes exist for submit, withdraw, start review, return for info, resubmit, decide, get by id, get by reference, and list by citizen.
Every business-rule error reaches the client with its code and message and an HTTP 4xx status. Validation and state errors return 4xx too.
The server adds no business rules. All lifecycle behaviour comes from src/requests.js.
The existing 41 tests still pass. Route handlers have their own tests.
src/requests.js exports a reviewer queue of SUBMITTED requests and an active-review count per reviewer. Each export has tests.
The server binds to loopback by default. Every screen shows a visible banner that says this is a fictional demo with no sign-in.
A citizen screen lets a person submit, withdraw, and resubmit a request. It shows that person's requests with status and history.
A reviewer screen lets a person start a review, return with a note, approve, or reject. It shows their active-review load against the limit.
Every status has a distinct visual marker. The history, including return notes, is visible per request.
Errors from the server appear on screen with their message. No failure is silent.
The layout is consistent across both screens and usable at phone width.
